clusters.name: Code Generation
clusters.description: User asks the model to write, complete, scaffold, or debug-fix source code: functions, classes, scripts, SQL queries, regexes, and small programs across languages.
exemplars: Write a Python function that takes a list of integers and returns the median without using statistics.median.
I need a TypeScript function `debounce(fn, ms)` that works with async functions and preserves the last call's arguments.
Create a SQL query that finds all customers who placed more than 3 orders in the last 90 days, along with their total spend.
Write a Rust function that parses a string like "key1=value1;key2=value2" into a HashMap, returning an error on malformed pairs.
Scaffold a small Express.js REST endpoint POST /users that validates an email and age field and returns 400 on bad input.
Write a Python script that walks a directory recursively and prints the 10 largest files with their sizes in human-readable form.
Implement a function in Go that merges two sorted slices into one sorted slice in O(n).

Here's my broken function:

def flatten(lst):
    result = []
    for i in lst:
        result.extend(i)
    return result

It crashes on flat lists like [1,2,3]. Fix it so it handles both nested and flat input.
Write a regex in JavaScript that validates a semver string like 1.2.3 or 2.0.0-rc.1.
Create a Python dataclass for a shopping cart with methods add_item, remove_item, and total (items have price and quantity).
Write a bash one-liner that finds all .log files older than 30 days and compresses them into a single archive.
Implement binary search in C++ that returns the index of the first element >= target, or -1 if none exists.
Write a Java method that converts a camelCase string to snake_case.
I need a Python generator that yields rows from a CSV file lazily, skipping blank lines and comment lines starting with #.
Write a React component `CopyButton` that copies given text to the clipboard and shows a checkmark for 2 seconds.
Create a SQL migration that adds a `status` enum column to the `tickets` table with values open/pending/closed, defaulting to open.
Write a Python function using requests that retries a GET up to 3 times with exponential backoff on 5xx responses.
Implement a simple LRU cache class in Python with O(1) get and put, using collections.OrderedDict.
Write a TypeScript type-level utility `DeepPartial<T>` and a small demo showing it applied to a nested config object.
Generate a Python function that validates an IBAN checksum using the mod-97 algorithm.
Write a Node.js script that reads a JSON file, increments a "version" field, and writes it back atomically (write to temp file then rename).
Implement Dijkstra's shortest path in Python for a graph represented as {node: [(neighbor, weight), ...]}.
Write a Kotlin extension function on String that truncates to N chars and appends an ellipsis only if it was cut.
Create a pytest suite with fixtures for a function `divide(a, b)` covering normal division, division by zero, and type errors.
Write a Python decorator that logs the function name, arguments, and execution time to stdout.
I need a C function that reverses a null-terminated string in place.
Write a GraphQL schema (SDL) for a blog with Post, Author, and Comment types plus a query to fetch a post with its comments.

clusters.name: Code Review
clusters.description: User pastes existing code or a diff and asks for review: bug finding, security audit, style/readability feedback, performance concerns, or refactor suggestions.
exemplars:
Review this function for bugs:

def get_user_age(user):
    return 2024 - user['birth_year']

I'm worried about edge cases.

Please review this SQL query for performance — it runs on a table with 50M rows:

SELECT * FROM orders WHERE LOWER(email) LIKE '%@example.com';

Code review request: this React component re-renders way too often. What am I doing wrong? const List = ({items}) => { const sorted = items.sort(); return
    {sorted.map(i =>
  • {i}
    • )}
; }

Review this PR: it adds password reset. Flag anything you'd block on, especially around token handling.

+ token = str(uuid4())[:8]
+ cache.set(f'reset:{email}', token)
+ send_email(email, f'Your code: {token}')

Can you critique this Rust code for style and idiomatic-ness? It works but feels clunky:

fn count_words(s: String) -> usize { let mut n = 0; for w in s.split(" ") { if w.len() > 0 { n = n + 1; } } n }

Please review this C snippet for memory safety:

char* greet(char* name) { char buf[64]; strcpy(buf, "Hello "); strcat(buf, name); return buf; }

Review this diff for a rate limiter — is the sliding window logic correct?

+ now = time()
+ self.hits = [t for t in self.hits if now - t < 60]
+ if len(self.hits) >= LIMIT: return False
+ self.hits.append(now)
+ return True

I wrote this validation function; review it for gaps an attacker could exploit:

function isValidUrl(u) { return u.startsWith('http'); }

Review this JavaScript for readability and suggest a cleaner structure:

if (user) { if (user.isActive) { if (user.role === 'admin') { doAdminThing(); } else { doUserThing(); } } else { redirect('/inactive'); } }

Please review this Go code — I'm seeing occasional goroutine leaks in production:

for _, job := range jobs { go func() { results <- process(job) }() }

Review this TypeScript function for type safety and edge cases:

function parseConfig(json: any) { return { port: json.port || 3000, debug: json.debug }; }

Review this Dockerfile and point out security and size issues:

FROM ubuntu:latest
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3
COPY . /app
CMD python3 /app/server.py

Here's a shell script I wrote. Review it for quoting/expansion bugs:

for f in $(ls /data/*.csv); do cp $f /backup/; done

Please review this Python multiprocessing code for deadlock risks:

with Pool(4) as p:
    results = [p.apply_async(worker, (q,)) for _ in range(8)]
    q.put('done')

Review this migration for a zero-downtime deploy — anything that will lock the table?

ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN last_login TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now();

Review this C++ code for undefined behavior:

int& get_first(std::vector<int>& v) { return v[0]; }

Here's my websocket handler. Review it for resource cleanup issues:

ws.on('message', async (msg) => { const db = await connect(); const r = await db.query(msg); ws.send(r); });

clusters.name: Summarization
clusters.description: User provides a long text (article, thread, transcript, ticket history, report) and asks for a summary, TL;DR, key points, or digest.
exemplars:
Summarize this article in 3 sentences:

[Article text about a city council approving a new light-rail line after years of debate, including budget figures and construction timeline...]
Give me a TL;DR of this 40-message email thread about the office relocation. I mainly care about the final decision and open questions.
Summarize the key takeaways from this meeting transcript. Bullet points please, and flag any decisions that were made.
Here's a long bug ticket with 25 comments. Summarize what the root cause turned out to be and what fix was merged.
Condense this 8-page incident postmortem into a half-page executive summary covering impact, cause, and action items.

Summarize this research abstract for a non-specialist audience in plain language:

"We evaluate contrastive fine-tuning of sentence encoders under low-resource regimes..."
I missed the all-hands. Here's the transcript — summarize the product roadmap updates and anything mentioned about hiring.
Turn this changelog into a short release-notes summary a customer would actually read.
Summarize this RFC document in 5 bullets, focusing on the API changes and the deprecation timeline.
Give me a one-paragraph summary of this customer feedback survey dump — what are the top 3 complaints?
Summarize this long forum thread about electric-vehicle battery degradation. What does the community consensus seem to be?
Here's a 3,000-word blog post about database indexing. Summarize it into a cheat-sheet of do's and don'ts.
Summarize this contract in plain English, highlighting obligations, payment terms, and termination conditions.
Condense this quarterly sales report into 4 bullet points I can paste into the board deck.

Summarize the plot of this short story in two sentences without spoiling the twist ending:

[story text]
I have 60 lines of Slack discussion about a production outage. Summarize the timeline of what happened and when.
Summarize this scientific news article about coral reef restoration in under 100 words for our newsletter.
Here's a verbose pull request description. Give me a two-sentence summary for the merge commit message.
Summarize this user manual section into quick-start steps for someone who just wants to get running in 5 minutes.
Digest this analyst report on the chip industry into the 3 most important trends with one line each.
Summarize this lecture transcript on photosynthesis for a high-school study guide.
Give me a structured summary (problem, approach, results) of this engineering design doc.
Summarize this long customer support chat — what did the customer want, what was offered, and how did it end?
Here's a podcast transcript about sleep science. Pull out a summary of the actionable advice given.
Summarize this terms-of-service update diff in plain language: what actually changed for users?
Condense this 12-message requirements discussion into a crisp list of agreed requirements and deferred items.
Summarize this book chapter in 5 bullet points capturing the main argument of each section.

clusters.name: Classification
clusters.description: User asks the model to assign labels or categories to text: sentiment, intent, topic, spam, toxicity, priority, or routing into a fixed label set.
exemplars: Classify the sentiment of this review as positive, negative, or mixed: "The battery life is amazing, but the screen scratches way too easily."

Label each of these support tickets by intent (billing, bug_report, feature_request, account_access, other):
1. "I was charged twice this month."
2. "The app crashes when I upload a PDF."
3. "Can you add dark mode?"
Is this email spam or legitimate? "CONGRATULATIONS!! You've been selected to claim a $1000 gift card. Act now!!!"
Classify this headline into one of: politics, sports, technology, health, entertainment. "New chiplet design cuts datacenter power draw by 30%."
Rate the toxicity of this comment as none, mild, or severe: "You're an idiot if you think that framework is any good. Uninstall and learn to code."
Classify the urgency of this IT ticket (low, medium, high, critical): "The payroll export fails for everyone and payday is tomorrow."
Tag this customer message with the right department — sales, support, or billing: "Hi, I want to upgrade our plan to cover 50 seats. What would that cost?"

Classify each sentence as a question, request, or complaint:
1. "Where is my refund?"
2. "Please cancel my subscription."
3. "Your checkout page is broken again."
Determine whether this product review is about quality, shipping, price, or customer service: "It took three weeks to arrive and the box was crushed."
Label this tweet's stance toward the new transit plan: support, oppose, or neutral. "The plan has some flaws but honestly it's the first credible attempt in years."
Classify this log message by severity (debug, info, warning, error): "Cache miss ratio exceeded 0.8 for the last 5 minutes."
Is this user message a churn risk signal? Answer yes/no with a one-word justification: "We've started evaluating alternatives since your pricing change."

Classify these news blurbs as world, business, or science:
1. "Central bank holds rates steady."
2. "Astronomers image a planet-forming disk in unprecedented detail."
Assign a topic category to this search query from the list [recipe, travel, finance, fitness, coding]: "how to knead sourdough without a stand mixer"
Classify the tone of this customer email as angry, frustrated, neutral, or satisfied: "This is the third time I'm writing. Nothing has been fixed and nobody has replied."
Label this code comment as TODO, FIXME, NOTE, or HACK based on its content: "temporary workaround until upstream fixes the race condition"
Classify this resume bullet by skill category (engineering, leadership, communication, analysis): "Mentored 4 junior engineers; two were promoted within a year."
Does this message contain a request for a refund? Answer true or false: "I'd like to return the jacket; it doesn't fit. What are my options?"
Classify this forum post by programming language: "Why does my list comprehension throw a KeyError when the dict is empty?"
Mark this sentence as sarcastic or sincere: "Great, another meeting that could have been an email. My favorite."
Classify the primary emotion in this journal entry (joy, sadness, anger, fear, surprise): "I keep checking my phone, waiting for news, and my hands won't stop shaking."
Categorize this expense description into travel, meals, equipment, or software: "Annual renewal of design tool licenses for the team."
Label this headline as clickbait or not: "You won't believe what this mayor said about parking!"
Classify this bug report by component (UI, API, database, infra): "The dashboard chart flickers and resets its zoom whenever data refreshes."
Is this text AI-generated or human-written? Give a label plus one-line rationale: [two paragraphs of generic marketing copy]
Classify the reading level of this passage as elementary, middle-school, high-school, or adult: [short passage about how bees communicate]

clusters.name: Multi-Step Reasoning
clusters.description: User poses problems requiring chained reasoning: math word problems, logic puzzles, constraint-based planning, scheduling, and comparative calculations.
exemplars: A train leaves Station A at 9:15 going 80 km/h. Another leaves Station B (300 km away) at 9:45 going 100 km/h toward A. At what time do they meet?
I have 8 coins and one is slightly heavier. Using a balance scale, what's the minimum number of weighings to guarantee finding it, and how?
If a shirt is discounted 25% and then an additional 10% off the sale price, and I pay $54, what was the original price?

Three friends — Ana, Bo, and Cy — each have a different pet (cat, dog, fish) and live on different floors (1, 2, 3). Ana doesn't live on floor 1. The dog owner lives on floor 3. Bo owns the cat. Who lives where?
Plan a 4-day trip to Lisbon with a $900 budget covering lodging, food, and activities. Break down the daily spending.
If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, how long would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets? Explain your reasoning.
A rectangle's length is twice its width. If the perimeter is 36 cm, what is the area?
I need to schedule 6 meetings into 3 rooms over a day. Meetings A and B can't overlap, C needs the large room, and D must come after E. Propose a valid schedule.
A bat and a ball cost $1.10 total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost? Show the algebra.
You have a 3-liter jug and a 5-liter jug. How do you measure exactly 4 liters? List each step.
If f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² - 1, what is f(g(2)) + g(f(0))? Walk through it step by step.
A store sells pens in packs of 4 for $5 or packs of 7 for $8. I need at least 30 pens at minimum cost. What should I buy?
Alice is taller than Bob. Carol is shorter than Dana. Bob is taller than Dana. Who is the shortest? Justify with the chain of comparisons.
How many ways can you arrange the letters in the word LEVEL? Show the counting argument.
A recipe for 4 people uses 300g of flour and 2 eggs. I'm cooking for 7 people but only have 3 eggs. Can I do it, and how should I scale the flour?
I can afford a car payment of $400/month for 48 months at 6% APR. Roughly what's the maximum loan amount I can take?
Two pipes fill a tank in 3 hours and 6 hours respectively. A drain empties it in 4 hours. If all three are open, does the tank fill, and how long does it take?
Given these constraints — no meetings before 10am, lunch 12–1, the client only free after 2pm, and the review needs 90 minutes — propose the earliest possible agenda for tomorrow.
If yesterday was the day after Wednesday's tomorrow, what day is today? Explain.
A number is divisible by 3, leaves remainder 1 when divided by 4, and is between 20 and 40. What is it?
My investment grew 20% in year 1 and fell 15% in year 2. If I started with $10,000, what's the net result and overall percentage change?
Five runners finished a race. Kai finished before Lee but after Mina. Tom finished right after Lee. Sam finished last. Give the full ordering.
A password uses 2 letters followed by 3 digits, no repeats. How many possible passwords are there? Show the multiplication.
I'm tiling a 12x10 ft floor with 2x1 ft tiles and each tile costs $3.50. Tax is 8%. What's the total cost?
If all Bloops are Razzies and all Razzies are Lazzies, are all Bloops definitely Lazzies? What if some Lazzies are not Razzies — does that change anything?
Work out the probability of rolling a sum of 8 with two fair dice, and compare it to the probability of a sum of 7.

clusters.name: Creative Writing
clusters.description: User asks for original creative content: stories, poems, slogans, jokes, song lyrics, worldbuilding, character sketches, and fictional dialogue.
exemplars: Write a short story (about 500 words) about a lighthouse keeper who receives a letter meant for someone a century ago.
Compose a haiku about the first snowfall in a city that rarely gets snow.
Give me 10 catchy slogans for a startup that delivers houseplants by subscription.
Write a poem in free verse about watching a parent grow old, from the child's perspective.
Invent a fantasy world where magic is powered by forgotten memories. Describe the society, its laws, and one everyday consequence of this system.
Write a funny dialogue between a cat and a Roomba who both believe they own the house.
Create a character sketch for a villain who genuinely believes they're the hero — a city planner in a cyberpunk setting.
Write the opening paragraph of a mystery novel set on a night train crossing the mountains in winter.
Write a children's bedtime story about a small dragon who's afraid of the dark.
Compose a sea shanty about a crew of programmers shipping a product launch.
Write a monologue for a stage play: an old chess champion explaining why they threw the final match.
Create 5 taglines for a fictional noir detective board game called 'Ashes & Alibis'.
Write a love poem that uses only imagery from astronomy — no clichés like 'stars in your eyes'.
Invent a mythology: tell the creation myth of a desert people who worship two rival moons.
Write a 150-word flash fiction piece where the twist is that the narrator is a house.
Come up with names and one-line backstories for 6 tavern patrons in a fantasy RPG.
Write a parody weather forecast for a planet where it rains metal and the wind blows at 400 km/h.
Compose a lullaby a robot parent might sing to its child about defragmenting dreams.
Write a scene where two rival food-truck owners negotiate a truce over the last parking spot at a festival.
Create a fictional dictionary entry (word, pronunciation, definition, example sentence) for the feeling of almost remembering a dream.
Write a ghost story told entirely through a series of voicemail transcripts.
Give me a sonnet about procrastination that ironically never quite gets to the point.
Invent three unusual superheroes whose powers are mildly inconvenient, and describe their day jobs.
Write the lyrics for a folk song about a town that votes to move itself one mile down the road.
Describe a floating city in enough detail for a novel's setting chapter: architecture, economy, and what it smells like at dawn.
Write a comedic breakup letter from a person to their smartphone.

clusters.name: Rewriting & Editing

Change the tone of this customer reply from defensive to apologetic: "As stated in our policy, which you agreed to, refunds after 30 days are not possible. There is nothing further we can do."

Rewrite this in passive voice: "The committee rejected the proposal after a lengthy debate."

Rewrite this resume bullet to be more achievement-oriented: "Responsible for handling customer complaints at the call center."

Fix the dangling modifier and comma splices: "Running late for the meeting, the slides were printed quickly, they were full of typos however nobody noticed."
Translate the formality level of this text down to casual chat register: "We regret to inform you that your reservation could not be accommodated at the requested time."

Rewrite this instruction as a numbered step-by-step list: "First you'll want to turn off the power and then after that unscrew the panel, being careful with the wires, then swap the fuse and put it all back."

Make this abstract more engaging for a general audience blog post, keeping it accurate:

"Results indicate a statistically significant reduction in recall latency under spaced-repetition conditions."
Reword this so it doesn't sound accusatory: "You missed the deadline again and now the whole team is blocked."

clusters.name: RAG Question Answering
clusters.description: User provides context passages or document excerpts inline and asks a question that must be answered strictly from that context.
exemplars:
Answer using only the context below.

Context: The Cedar Falls library is open Monday–Friday 9am–8pm and Saturdays 10am–4pm. It is closed on Sundays and public holidays. The children's wing closes 30 minutes before the main building.

Question: Can I visit the children's wing at 4:30pm on a Saturday?

Based on this policy excerpt, how many vacation days does a 3-year employee get?

Policy: Employees accrue vacation as follows: 0–1 years of service: 10 days/year. 1–5 years: 15 days/year. Over 5 years: 20 days/year.

Using the provided changelog, which version introduced dark mode?

Changelog: v2.1 — fixed export bug, improved startup time. v2.2 — added dark mode and custom themes. v2.3 — performance fixes; removed legacy importer.

Answer from the passage only: What caused the bridge closure?

Passage: The Harton Bridge closed on March 3 after inspectors found corrosion on two load-bearing cables. Repairs are expected to take eight weeks; detours via Route 9 are posted.

Given the product specs below, does the drone support 4K recording?

Specs: SkyHawk Mini — weight 249g, flight time 31 min, camera: 2.7K at 30fps, 1080p at 60fps, 12MP stills.

Read the FAQ excerpt and answer: what is the refund window for digital purchases?

FAQ: Physical items may be returned within 30 days of delivery. Digital purchases are refundable within 14 days of purchase, provided they have not been downloaded. Subscriptions can be cancelled anytime but are non-refundable.

From this onboarding doc, what's the first thing a new engineer should do?

Doc: Day one checklist: 1) Pick up your laptop from IT (building B, floor 2). 2) Set up your dev environment using the setup script in the eng repo. 3) Join the #eng-new-hires channel.

Using only the meeting notes, what deadline was set for the design freeze?

clusters.name: Agentic Tool Use
clusters.description: User asks the assistant to do something in the world via tools/APIs: check calendars, query databases, call services, book things, search the web, send messages, or manage files and tickets.
exemplars: Check my calendar for tomorrow and move any meeting that conflicts with the dentist appointment at 2pm.
Query the analytics database for weekly active users over the last 8 weeks and tell me if the trend is up or down.
Search the web for the current price of a round-trip flight from Austin to Denver leaving next Friday, then email me the cheapest option.
Create a Jira ticket for the login-page crash, assign it to the on-call engineer, and link it to the incident channel thread.
Look up the weather forecast for Saturday and, if it's going to rain, reschedule the team picnic event to the following Saturday and notify attendees.
Call the payments API to refund order #4471 for the full amount and then update the order status in the admin panel.
Find all files in the shared drive modified in the last week that mention 'Q3 roadmap' and compile them into a folder for me.
Book a conference room for 6 people on Tuesday from 10 to 11:30, ideally one with a whiteboard and video setup.
Monitor the deploy pipeline and, once the staging build goes green, trigger the production deploy and post a message in #releases.
Run a SQL query against the warehouse to find the top 20 customers by lifetime value, then export the result as a CSV to my desktop.
Search our internal docs for the VPN setup guide and add its link to the new-hire checklist in the wiki.
Check the inventory system: if the SKU 'WB-1042' is below 50 units, create a purchase order for 200 more and ping the procurement channel.
Fetch the latest error logs from the production cluster, group them by error type, and open a ticket for any type with more than 100 occurrences today.
Schedule a recurring 1:1 with my manager every other Wednesday at 3pm, starting next week, and add an agenda doc link to each invite.
Use the maps API to find the three coffee shops nearest to the office that open before 7am, and add them to the team doc.
Pull the latest build artifact from CI, upload it to the release bucket, and update the download link on the docs site.
Look up the current exchange rate between USD and EUR, then update the pricing spreadsheet's currency column accordingly.
Search GitHub for open PRs older than 5 days in our repo and send a gentle reminder message to each reviewer assigned.
Check whether the SSL certificate for our staging domain expires within 30 days; if so, file an ops ticket to renew it.
Order a replacement keyboard through the IT procurement portal using my saved cost center, and confirm the delivery date back to me.
Query the CRM for all leads in the 'contacted' stage with no activity in 14 days and draft a follow-up email for each one.
Set a reminder for 15 minutes before every one of my meetings this week, and text me a daily agenda at 8am each morning.
Scrape the competitor's changelog page weekly and diff it against last week's version; alert me if they shipped anything new.
Reserve a table for four at a well-reviewed Italian restaurant near the theater for 6pm Friday, then add it to my calendar with the address.
Check the status of our three cloud instances and restart any that have been unreachable for more than 5 minutes.
Use the email API to send the signed contract PDF to the vendor, then mark the deal as 'closed-won' in the pipeline tracker.
